stringr ::: {.column} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](images/stringr-tidyverse.png){fig-align='center' width=80%} ::: ::: ::: :::: {.column} ::: {.incremental} Functions to work with strings - detect matches - subset strings - manage lengths - mutate strings - join and split strings ::: :::: ## Typical stringr function format Most string functions are in the format: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|1|2|3|"} func_name( string, pattern, ... ) ``` ::: ## Detect matches {.smaller} `string_detect(string, pattern)`: Detects the presence of a pattern match in a string ::: column ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} starwars %>% select(name, hair_color) %>% filter(hair_color == "brown") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 18 × 2 name hair_color 1 Leia Organa brown 2 Beru Whitesun Lars brown 3 Chewbacca brown 4 Han Solo brown 5 Wedge Antilles brown 6 Jek Tono Porkins brown 7 Arvel Crynyd brown 8 Wicket Systri Warrick brown 9 Qui-Gon Jinn brown 10 Padmé Amidala brown 11 Ric Olié brown 12 Cordé brown 13 Cliegg Lars brown 14 Dormé brown 15 Tarfful brown 16 Raymus Antilles brown 17 Rey brown 18 Poe Dameron brown ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: column ::: fragment ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} starwars %>% select(name, hair_color) %>% filter(str_detect(hair_color,"brown")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 19 × 2 name hair_color 1 Leia Organa brown 2 Owen Lars brown, grey 3 Beru Whitesun Lars brown 4 Chewbacca brown 5 Han Solo brown 6 Wedge Antilles brown 7 Jek Tono Porkins brown 8 Arvel Crynyd brown 9 Wicket Systri Warrick brown 10 Qui-Gon Jinn brown 11 Padmé Amidala brown 12 Ric Olié brown 13 Cordé brown 14 Cliegg Lars brown 15 Dormé brown 16 Tarfful brown 17 Raymus Antilles brown 18 Rey brown 19 Poe Dameron brown ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Subset strings {.smaller} `str_sub(string, start, end)`: Subset strings based on a known location `str_extract(string, pattern)`: Return the first pattern match found ::: column ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} starwars %>% select(name, hair_color) %>% mutate(primary_hair = str_sub(hair_color, 1, 5)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 87 × 3 name hair_color primary_hair 1 Luke Skywalker blond blond 2 C-3PO 3 R2-D2 4 Darth Vader none none 5 Leia Organa brown brown 6 Owen Lars brown, grey brown 7 Beru Whitesun Lars brown brown 8 R5-D4 9 Biggs Darklighter black black 10 Obi-Wan Kenobi auburn, white aubur # ℹ 77 more rows ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: column ::: fragment ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} starwars %>% select(name, hair_color) %>% mutate(primary_hair = str_extract(hair_color, "^.*,")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 87 × 3 name hair_color primary_hair 1 Luke Skywalker blond 2 C-3PO 3 R2-D2 4 Darth Vader none 5 Leia Organa brown 6 Owen Lars brown, grey brown, 7 Beru Whitesun Lars brown 8 R5-D4 9 Biggs Darklighter black 10 Obi-Wan Kenobi auburn, white auburn, # ℹ 77 more rows ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Regular expressions Powerful...yet annoying . . . A few common ones you will likely use: | operator | definition | | operator | definition | |----------|------------------------|----|------------|------------------------| | `^` | start of a string | | `[:alpha:]` | all upper and lower case alpha characters | | `$` | end of a string | | `[:digit:]` | all numeric digits | | `.` | any character | | `[:alnum:]` | all `[:alpha:]` + all `[:digit:]` | | `a*` | zero or more "a" in a row | | `[abe]` | one of the letters in brackets | | `a{n}` | exactly n "a" characters in a row | | `[^abe]` | anything but the letters in brackets | . . . When I work with strings, the [stringr cheatsheet](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/strings.pdf) is always open in a browser (or on my desk)! ## Subset strings {.smaller} `str_extract(string, pattern)`: Return the first pattern match found ::: column ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} starwars %>% select(name, hair_color) %>% mutate(primary_hair = str_extract(hair_color, "^.*,")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 87 × 3 name hair_color primary_hair 1 Luke Skywalker blond 2 C-3PO 3 R2-D2 4 Darth Vader none 5 Leia Organa brown 6 Owen Lars brown, grey brown, 7 Beru Whitesun Lars brown 8 R5-D4 9 Biggs Darklighter black 10 Obi-Wan Kenobi auburn, white auburn, # ℹ 77 more rows ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: column ::: fragment ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} starwars %>% select(name, hair_color) %>% mutate(primary_hair = str_extract(hair_color, "^.*(?=,)")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 87 × 3 name hair_color primary_hair 1 Luke Skywalker blond 2 C-3PO 3 R2-D2 4 Darth Vader none 5 Leia Organa brown 6 Owen Lars brown, grey brown 7 Beru Whitesun Lars brown 8 R5-D4 9 Biggs Darklighter black 10 Obi-Wan Kenobi auburn, white auburn # ℹ 77 more rows ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Mutate strings `str_replace(string, pattern, replacement)`: Replace the first matched patttern ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} starwars %>% select(name, hair_color) %>% mutate(new_hair = str_replace(hair_color, "blond", "rainbow")) %>% filter(str_detect(hair_color,"blond")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4 × 3 name hair_color new_hair 1 Luke Skywalker blond rainbow 2 Anakin Skywalker blond rainbow 3 Finis Valorum blond rainbow 4 Zam Wesell blonde rainbowe ``` ::: ::: ## Mutate strings (cont.) `str_replace(string, pattern, replacement)`: Replace the first matched patttern ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} starwars %>% select(name, hair_color) %>% mutate(additional_colors = str_replace(hair_color, "^.*, ", "")) %>% filter(str_detect(hair_color,",")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 3 × 3 name hair_color additional_colors 1 Owen Lars brown, grey grey 2 Obi-Wan Kenobi auburn, white white 3 Wilhuff Tarkin auburn, grey grey ``` ::: ::: ## Split strings `str_split_i(string, pattern, n)`: Split at the pattern, and return the nth substring ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} starwars %>% select(name, hair_color) %>% mutate(additional_colors = str_split_i(hair_color, ", ", 2)) %>% filter(str_detect(hair_color,",")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 3 × 3 name hair_color additional_colors 1 Owen Lars brown, grey grey 2 Obi-Wan Kenobi auburn, white white 3 Wilhuff Tarkin auburn, grey grey ``` ::: ::: ## Other helpful string functions ::: {.incremental} - `str_length(string)`: number of characters (also `nchar(string)`) - `str_pad(string, width, side, pad = " ")`: pad the string with additional characters (default is to pad with a space, but can also use this to pad leading 0s) - `str_trim(string, side)`: trim whitespace from the start and/or end of a string - `str_squish(string)`: trim whitespace from both ends and collapse multiple spaces in the middle into a single space - `toupper(string)`: converts the entire string to uppercase - `tolower(string)`: converts the entire string to lowercase ::: # Your turn:

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
